# Review of beowulf-fitt-03 (units.json)

Two passes. Pass 1: the full order of checks (labels, OE to l, l to i, remembered English, house consistency). Pass 2: re-read the edited file, mechanical scan (spelling, workflow words, name of the hero, note length 12-150), and the residual checks. `t`, `ln`, `v`, `p` verified byte-identical to the draft before and after. `gloss.json` did not exist at review time, so the glossary parse check could not be done; it must be checked in the second pass once the glosser has run.

Severity: high = a false label or a wrong sense that would mislead the reader; medium = l/i/n disagreement, unflagged guess, unsupported claim; low = style, spelling, house consistency.

## Considered and refused

- 189 n 'mǣlceare is a dative of means' and 'sēað is past tense of sēoþan': checked, true (sēoþan, sēað, sudon). 'time-care' is already flagged as a guess. Kept.
- 190 n 'the verb mihte takes a bare infinitive, and the object wēan comes between them': checked against the line (ne mihte snotọr hæleð wēan onwendan). Kept. The dot-under-vowel explanation occurs once, here, at the first dotted vowel of the part (snotọr, 190); 219 refers back to it. Kept.
- 191 n 'þē after the comma is a relative particle ... verb becōm': true of the line. i attaches the relative to 'oppression' while the note attaches it to 'struggle'; the Old English allows both, so left.
- 194 'Þæt ... Grendles dǣda' as object plus explanatory apposition: true; dǣda is accusative plural. Kept.
- 196 n 'ēacen is the past participle of ēacan': true.
- 198 n 'Hēt takes an accusative and an infinitive'; 'him' as dative of interest: true of the form; the reflexive reading is also possible but gives the same English. The kenning explanation was not removed: ȳðlida is not the first kenning of the poem, but the note only defines the term in one sentence and the convention allows a nudge.
- 199 n gūðcyning and mǣrne þēoden 'accusative singular': mǣrne is unambiguous, gūðcyning has the same form in nominative and accusative; taken as accusative by apposition. Kept.
- 202 n 'wǣre is subjunctive': true (preterite subjunctive after þēah). i 'though he was dear to them' renders the mood as plain English; kept.
- 204 n on the Thorkelin transcripts A and B: apparatus gives 'A þofne, B forne' for the second element only; the note reports that. Kept.
- 207 n '.xv.' with 'na' above: matches the apparatus. Kept.
- 217 gefȳsed, winde as dative of means, gelīc with the dative: true.
- 218-219 'dōgọres' dot: back-reference is correct (explanation not repeated).
- 226 'sǣldon from sǣlian': accepted (sǣl rope); flagged nowhere because it is the standard analysis.
- 227 n 'Gode is a dative since þancian takes the dative': true.
- 229 'weall may mean a cliff-face or an earthwork': already hedged. Kept.
- 232 i 'Curiosity ... to know' was replaced, not refused (see changes).
- 237 'Hwæt' as question word versus the call for attention in 240: both are distinguished in the notes; l keeps 'What' in both, i switches only where the bracketed text may be the call. Kept; no house-rendering conflict ('Hwæt' = 'What!' in l, 'Listen!' in i applies to the call for attention; 237 is the pronoun).
- 237 i 'Who are you' for 'hwæt syndon gē': the note already explains 'what (kind)'; natural English. Kept.
- 240 i 'I have been' for 'wæs' (preterite): idiomatic in direct speech with 'for a while'; kept.
- 254 n 'gehȳrað is the plural imperative': the form is identical to the present plural indicative, but the vocative and the colon force the imperative. Unlike 'wǣron' (232), where the mood cannot be read from context, this label is true of the form in the line. Kept.
- 'foamy-necked' (217-218): a literal rendering of fāmīheals built from the compound; no change. 'Haste is best', 'a man in his armor': built from the grammar; no echo suspected.
- Beowulf is named nowhere in the units (scan: none). Hrothgar is named in the note at 189 only as an identification of 'maga Healfdenes', which Fitt I supports. Kept.
- Single curly quotes and plain sentences: scanned; no straight or double quotes used as quotation marks in notes.
- Consistency with published parts: 'lāþ ond longsum' ('loathsome and long-lasting' in l, as Fitt II), 'wine'/'hæleð' not in conflict, 'byrnies' aligned, 'Scyldings', 'Geats', 'Weders', 'hronrād' back-reference, 'bearm' back-reference, 'næs hit lengra fyrst' and 'morðbealu' (Fitt II 134-135) back-references all verified against the published text.

## Residual points for the glosser or the next reader

- Fitt I and II glossary entry for 'gefrægn' reads 'I heard tell (1st singular)'; in this part it is 3rd singular (194). The glosser should broaden it.
- 'lēode' and the lēod 'prince' reading at 205 depend on the glossary parse; check against gloss.json when it exists.
